title: Lateral Attenuation of Evapotranspiration‐Driven Groundwater Fluctuations: Implications for Saturated Hydraulic Conductivity
content:
Evapotranspiration induces diurnal groundwater fluctuations that propagate laterally and attenuate with distance. The attenuation coefficient is obtained from the linear relationship between logarithmic fluctuation amplitude and distance. A numerically established relationship between this coefficient and K s −0.5 enables estimation of saturated hydraulic conductivity for a target aquifer material.


ABSTRACT

Saturated hydraulic conductivity (K s ) is a fundamental hydrogeological parameter controlling groundwater flow and solute transport. However, the potential of the attenuation of evapotranspiration-driven groundwater fluctuations for constraining this parameter remains insufficiently explored. To address this gap, this study develops an analytical framework and evaluates its implications using idealized two-dimensional HYDRUS simulations of a hillslope. The analytical model describes horizontal propagation outside a localized fluctuation source. Under this condition, the attenuation coefficient of groundwater level fluctuation amplitude constrains hydraulic diffusivity, whereas estimating K s additionally requires independent constraints on storage coefficient. Numerical simulations produced an approximately linear decrease in the logarithm of groundwater fluctuation amplitude with distance, with coefficients of determination approximately 0.985–0.993 across the six aquifer material scenarios. Strong relationships between the attenuation coefficient of groundwater level fluctuation amplitude and K s −0.5 persisted under the tested slope gradients, bottom fluxes, and evapotranspiration intensities. Leave-one-out cross-validation yielded an overall R 2 of 0.966 for the prescribed and predicted K s −0.5 values, indicating internal predictive consistency within the synthetic dataset. These results support the potential of the attenuation coefficient of groundwater level fluctuation amplitude as a constraint on aquifer hydraulic properties. The framework provides a basis for subsequent independent numerical and field testing.
